teacher_info.about_teacher:
For the past few years I have helped students to acquire fluency in the English language.
 It came to my attention that a lot of students who already speak the language at some level, feel the need to practice it in order to expand their vocabulary, improve their grammar and focus on their pronunciation. Therefore, Vocabulary, Grammar, and Pronunciation are, in my humble opinion, the three main pillars of a good and productive English conversation class.
teacher_info.teaching_style:
Since I only teach adults, one-on-one, (18+) Pre-Intermediate to Advanced levels I feel free to choose the tools used in our classes.

pro_course_detail.title: German Grammar and Conversation for Self-Learners
pro_course_detail.description:
Please Note: I don't offer structured German lessons for beginners. 

My goal is to help self-study students or those already taking some type of formal instruction.

I especially welcome learners having difficulty with German grammar. When I first started teaching myself, I realized I didn't understand the German grammatical terms and concepts. Then it dawned on me that I didn't really understand them in my native language, English, either. So I had to stop and learn all that before I could go any further. If you, like me, picked up your native language without thinking much about its grammar, I can help you learn what you need to know to understand German grammar.

Of course, understanding German grammar and being able to use it are two different things. If your goal is to speak German spontaneously and correctly, certain concepts and information must be internalized. There are various methods for accomplishing this, and the right way is the one that works best for you. As a self-learner, I tried virtually every resource I could get my hands on, so I can give you lots of suggestions.

In any case, I'll give you the opportunity to speak German as much as possible, either as a means of putting grammatical concepts into practice, or just for the fun of it.
